Same Rank, Fewer Clicks: An Early Warning for Pages Losing Google Clicks to AI Answers

Theresia Saumu November 2026

Click-through at a fixed position fell by about a third at the top of Google in six months. This paper measures it on FlyRank's warehouse, then asks whether a model can tell an editor which 50 pages to protect next month, honestly, on months it never saw.

AAbstract↑ Top

AI answers in search are the new variable in FlyRank's business, yet nobody had measured what they do to the clicks a page earns from Google at the rank it already holds. Using FlyRank's pseudonymized internship warehouse (78.8 million daily rows, January 2025 to June 2026), I estimate with page fixed effects and client-clustered errors that top-3 click-through in April 2026 was 0.642 times its October 2025 level for the same page in the same position band (95% CI 0.615 to 0.669); transactional pages fell more than informational ones. I then built a monthly ranking that tells an editor which top-10 pages are most likely to lose at least a quarter of their expected clicks over the next two months, using an observed label designed so that visible momentum cannot give it away, 34 engineered features, four frozen baselines, tuning nested inside training months, and forward validation with a sealed final month opened once. Across four forward months the logistic ranking put 0.42 to 0.66 eroding pages in a 50-page queue against base rates of 0.23 to 0.34, and it led every baseline on whole-ranking quality (PR-AUC) in all four months, while the best simple rule changed from month to month. The results are observational and decision-support only: Search Console has no AI-answer flag, so the click loss is consistent with AI answers rather than proven to be caused by them.

In one minute

Question
Which ranking pages will lose clicks at the rank they hold, so an editor can protect 50 of them first each month?
Finding
Same page, same position: top-3 CTR at 0.64× in six months; CTR fell in 10 of 11 clients.
Method
Leak-checked label, 34 features, four frozen rules, nested tuning, forward months, one sealed month.
Result
About twice the base rate in every forward month; best on PR-AUC in 4 of 4; the editor's intuitive rule failed out of sample.
Use
A reviewed monthly queue with reason codes. Predictive, not causal.

◆What the evidence supports↑ Top

Claim 1 · observed

At a fixed page and position, click-through fell after October 2025: 10 of 11 clients (median client ratio 0.664); top-3 at 0.642 by April 2026. Section 4.

Claim 2 · measured

Transactional pages fell to 0.677 [0.615, 0.746]; informational pages did not fall significantly (0.834 [0.537, 1.296]).

Claim 3 · decision support

The frozen ranking reached precision@50 of 0.42 on the sealed month (base 0.24) and led every baseline on PR-AUC in all four forward months.

Not claimed

That AI answers caused the fall, that the model beats the best rule at exactly 50 pages in every month (intervals overlap), or that acting on the queue restores clicks.

1Introduction↑ Top

FlyRank produces and maintains content for client sites, and AI answers in search (Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini) are changing what a ranking is worth. FlyRank's State of AI-Driven SEO 2026 report measures AI referral sessions, but not what AI answers do to Google clicks at a given rank. Industry studies report click-through falling where AI Overviews appear, but they use cross-sectional keyword samples, not a panel of client pages followed over time.

My earlier work on Lane 2 (refresh), archived in the repository, taught the lesson that shaped this study: when the label is largely answered by momentum that is already visible, a two-line rule beats any model. This study therefore starts with a target that momentum does not give away, and with the decision an editor faces: a budget of 50 reviews a month, and the question of which pages to protect before their clicks disappear.

What I excluded and why

  • Months before October 2025 for any comparison: Google's September 2025 removal of deep-result impressions shifted every position average (the share of impressions in the top 10 rose from 69% to 95%).
  • Pages outside the top 10, or with fewer than 200 impressions or 20 clicks in the feature window (their CTR is too noisy to judge).
  • Pages whose expected outcome clicks are under 10 (the label cannot be measured); this uses outcome impressions, so it is a disclosed population choice.
  • The 90-day query table: its window (April to June 2026) overlaps every outcome window.
  • The column provider_used, which contains brand-like strings; it is never selected.
  • AI-assistant referral sessions as a target: 83,618 sessions in total, only from October 2025, with two clients holding 68% of them.

3Methodology↑ Top

Label

At each monthly decision point, features use the two closed months before it and the label uses the two months after. A page erodes if its outcome clicks fall below 75% of what its current click-through predicts at its new position. "Current" is the latest month's CTR, shrunk toward the client's position-adjusted CTR, with a position curve fixed on October and November 2025. Two earlier label versions leaked momentum and made every model look better; both were fixed during development, before the sealed month was opened. A Poisson simulation puts the noise-only rate at 0.045 to 0.058, against observed base rates four to seven times higher.

Features, baselines and models

  • 34 features, exported from code: exposure, trajectory, rank, CTR against expectation, content, GA4 channels, client context and page history. Every one is computed from months that closed before the decision.
  • Four frozen baselines: the editor's rule (top position plus slipping CTR), CTR above peers, client-wide shock and persistence; plus random order.
  • Regularised logistic regression and gradient boosting, tuned with an inner GroupKFold by client inside training months only (scored by PR-AUC).

Validation

Forward months: each decision month trains only on months whose labels had matured. Primary metric: precision@50, next to the base rate, with 95% intervals from resampling clients. I froze the final model (logistic regression; reason recorded in the freeze receipt) and then opened the sealed month (outcome May to June 2026) once. A planted leak raises precision@50 from 0.66 to 1.00, which shows the harness can see leaks. A random row split overstates PR-AUC (0.538 against 0.422 with clients held out).

Reading the sealed month. The model reached 0.42 at 50 pages (CI 0.28 to 0.7) against 0.40 for the best baseline, whose 50 picks came from only 2 clients, and 0.38 for the editor's rule, whose AUC (0.453) was worse than random order. At exactly 50 pages the lead is inside the noise; on PR-AUC (0.348 against 0.234) and within-client precision@10 (0.50) it is clear.

4.3 What the model learned

The largest weights say that the pages losing clicks next are the ones currently earning more than their rank normally earns, or riding a recent CTR bump. That is the opposite of the editor's intuition ("slipping keeps slipping"). It matches the training-month signal checks, in which top-3 pages and slipping pages eroded less often, not more. A single-signal rule built on that idea alone ranks at about the base rate, so the edge comes from combining signals.

4.4 AI referrals and discovery

AI-assistant sessions are thin (83,618) and concentrated: 13,270 of 205,933 GA4-tracked pages ever received one. Within a client, the first AI referral follows exposure (prior impressions, AUC 0.715) and not Google rank (AUC 0.506).

5Limitations and honest framing↑ Top

  • Predictive, not causal. Search Console has no AI-answer flag. Seasonality, other search-feature changes and impression inflation are competing explanations for the click loss.
  • Four forward months only; intervals at 50 pages are wide (about ±0.2).
  • Eligibility keeps pages still in the top 10 with enough clicks, which favours survivors; measurability uses outcome impressions.
  • The top of the queue is dominated by pages with sudden impression swings, the main source of false alarms.
  • The per-client cap in the playbook was added after the sealed month was opened; its sealed effect is reported only as an observation.
  • Gradient boosting was not bit-reproducible across reruns on the development machine, one reason the logistic model was frozen.
Predictive, not causal. Decision support for human reviewers; no claim that acting on the queue changes traffic.

6Ranked recommendations↑ Top

1Protect before repairing. Each month, review the 50-page queue (at most 10 per client, pages at least 90 days old). Start with pages earning more than their rank normally earns: make them the source an AI answer cites (answer-first summary, FAQ, structured data) before any rewrite.
2Check the live results page first. Record whether an AI answer appears. If impressions jumped threefold or the page has one month of data, confirm demand before acting.
3Prioritise transactional and commercial pages in AI-search planning for this panel; informational pages did not show a significant fall.
4Do not use Google rank as a proxy for AI visibility. AI discovery followed exposure, not rank.
5Measure the action. Leave 10 of each month's 50 pages untouched and compare, so the value of the work can be estimated.
6Retrain monthly. Pause the queue if a matured month's precision falls below 1.3× its base rate.

July 2026 queue: 14,100 eligible pages; 50 queued across 7 clients; about 25,324 clicks at stake over two months if each lost a quarter.

7Reproducibility↑ Top

Code: work/scripts/, one module per stage. Notebooks: work/notebooks/, one per assignment card, executed with outputs. Receipts: work/outputs/*.json; every number on this page is read from them by make_paper.py. Seed 42; warehouse revision 50cbf7c3; freeze receipt with code hashes: erosion_freeze.json (frozen 2026-11-05).
